cli.update_help.update.tone: terse, operator-facing, preserves safety and command distinctions
cli.update_help.update.note: Top-level summary distinguishes PyPI upgrades from the local checkout rebuilding lop-update script; preserve the script name and PyPI brand.

cli.update_help.check.tone: terse, operator-facing, preserves safety and command distinctions
cli.update_help.check.note: --check compares the installed build with PyPI without installing anything. Preserve the flag token and PyPI brand.

cli.update_help.from_snapshot.tone: terse, operator-facing, preserves safety and command distinctions
cli.update_help.from_snapshot.note: --from-snapshot accepts a source directory or current-repository git ref. Preserve the macOS published-release wheel exception and its key-agent constraint; other refs build from source.

cli.update_help.allow_downgrade.tone: terse, operator-facing, preserves safety and command distinctions
cli.update_help.allow_downgrade.note: --allow-downgrade permits a deliberate rollback only with --from-snapshot, recorded in the marker. Preserve newer-only PyPI behavior and refresh-flag precedence.

cli.update_help.no_services.tone: terse, operator-facing, preserves safety and command distinctions
cli.update_help.no_services.note: --no-services skips bringing lop serve daemons onto the build, but supervised daemons are still repaired. Preserve this distinction and the lop serve command.

cli.update_help.no_roll.tone: terse, operator-facing, preserves safety and command distinctions
cli.update_help.no_roll.note: --no-roll suppresses the automatic mesh rollout regardless of network.rollout_on_update; lop network update remains available manually. Preserve config/command tokens.
